A0234.title: Embodied Data-Collection Privacy Protection
A0234.definition: Protecting privacy data collected by robot-mounted cameras/microphones in homes, malls, and factories via on-device processing, data desensitization, collection notice and consent, and differential privacy.
A0234.description: Embodied data collection privacy protection addresses incidents such as the iRobot Roomba J7 private image leak, Ecovacs robot vacuum remote eavesdropping, and Amazon Astro home surveillance by building safeguards across the data lifecycle. First, on-device processing ensures sensitive data (faces, voiceprints, home layouts) is inferred locally on the robot without uploading to the cloud. Second, data anonymization applies face blurring, voice alteration, and layout generalization to training or annotation data that must be uploaded. Third, collection notice and consent requires clear disclosure of collection scope and purpose to users and obtaining explicit consent before collection begins. Fourth, differential privacy adds noise to statistical data to prevent re-identification of individuals from aggregated data. This control works in conjunction with A0069 (Privacy Enhancing Technologies) and A0078 (Endpoint Detection and Response); the former provides general privacy techniques, while this control focuses on physical world collection scenarios specific to embodied devices, forming a core compliance requirement for embodied intelligence under GDPR and the Personal Information Protection Law.
A0234.limitation: On-device processing is constrained by device computing power, making local deployment of complex models difficult; anonymization may degrade training data value and impair model performance; notice and consent mechanisms risk becoming a mere formality, as users rarely truly understand the consequences of collection; differential privacy significantly reduces data utility in low-cardinality scenarios.
